[Cyclone Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Freddy "Cyclone Freddy") near Madagascar

*   [February 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_4 "February 4") – [Cyclone Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Freddy "Cyclone Freddy")[forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteorological_history_of_Cyclone_Freddy "Meteorological history of Cyclone Freddy") in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"). It would become the longest lasting [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") in history and [cause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_response_to_Cyclone_Freddy "Humanitarian response to Cyclone Freddy") over 1,400 deaths and countless injuries and property damage across southeastern Africa.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-Records-39)
*   [February 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_5 "February 5") – The [2023 Cypriot presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cypriot_presidential_election "2023 Cypriot presidential election") is held, with [Nikos Christodoulides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikos_Christodoulides "Nikos Christodoulides") elected [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Cyprus "President of Cyprus").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-:123-41)
*   [February 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_6 "February 6") – A 7.8 [M ww](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismic_magnitude_scales#Mww "Seismic magnitude scales")[earthquake strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Turkey%E2%80%93Syria_earthquakes "2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes") southern and central [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") and northern and western [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") followed by a 7.7 M ww aftershock on the same day, causing widespread damage and at more than 59,000 fatalities and 121,000 injured.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-TRdead22/42-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-D_6600-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-TRinjured-44)
*   [February 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_13 "February 13") – The [2023 Bangladeshi presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Bangladeshi_presidential_election "2023 Bangladeshi presidential election") scheduled for 19 February is held, with [Shahabuddin Chuppu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahabuddin_Chuppu "Shahabuddin Chuppu") of the [Awami League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awami_League "Awami League"), the only nominated candidate, elected unopposed.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-49)
*   [February 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_14 "February 14") – The [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") approves a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel [vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle") in the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") from 2035, citing the need to combat [climate change in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Europe "Climate change in Europe") and promote [electric vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_vehicle "Electric vehicle").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-50)
*   [February 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_16 "February 16") – Lawmakers in the [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia")[State Duma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Duma "State Duma") vote to withdraw Russia from 21 conventions of the [Council of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-51)
*   [February 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_17 "February 17") – The [South African Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Navy "South African Navy") hosts a 10-day joint [military exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_exercise "Military exercise") in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean") with [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-52)
*   [February 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_19 "February 19") – [Libyan Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libyan_Crisis_(2011%E2%80%93present) "Libyan Crisis (2011–present)"): The [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") announces the organization of a [peace conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_conference "Peace conference") to address the instability in [Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya "Libya").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-53)
*   [February 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_21 "February 21") – Vladimir Putin announces that Russia is suspending its participation in [New START](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_START "New START"), a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the US.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-54)
*   [February 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_23 "February 23") – [Oman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman "Oman") opens its [airspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airspace "Airspace") to [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")[airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_airlines_of_Israel "List of airlines of Israel") for the first time, in an upgrade of [bilateral relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Oman_relations "Israel–Oman relations").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-55)
*   [February 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_25 "February 25") – [2023 Nigerian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Nigerian_general_election "2023 Nigerian general election"): [Bola Tinubu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bola_Tinubu "Bola Tinubu") is elected as Nigeria's [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Nigeria "President of Nigeria"), defeating former [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_Nigeria "Vice President of Nigeria")[Atiku Abubakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atiku_Abubakar "Atiku Abubakar") and [Peter Obi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Obi "Peter Obi").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-Punch_Newspapers_2023-57)
*   [February 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_27 "February 27") – The United Kingdom and the European Union reach an [agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Framework "Windsor Framework") surrounding modifications to the [Northern Ireland Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_Protocol "Northern Ireland Protocol").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-58)
*   [February 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_28 "February 28") – A [train crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempi_train_crash "Tempi train crash") in [Thessaly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thessaly "Thessaly"), [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece"), kills 57 people and injures dozens. The crash leads to nationwide [protests and strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempi_train_crash_protests "Tempi train crash protests") against the condition of Greek railways and their mismanagement.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-60)

**From left to right, top to bottom:**
*   [ChatGPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT"), developed by [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI"), comes into widespread use;
*   Supporters of former [Brazilian president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil")[Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro")[storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Brazilian_Congress_attack "2023 Brazilian Congress attack") the [National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Congress_of_Brazil "National Congress of Brazil") following his defeat in the [2022 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Brazilian_general_election "2022 Brazilian general election");
*   A makeshift memorial to leaders of the [Wagner Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wagner_Group "Wagner Group"), who [died in a plane crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Wagner_Group_plane_crash "2023 Wagner Group plane crash") two months after [rebelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wagner_Group_rebellion "Wagner Group rebellion") against the [Russian government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_under_Vladimir_Putin "Russia under Vladimir Putin");
*   An alleged [high-altitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-altitude_balloon "High-altitude balloon")[observation balloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observation_balloon "Observation balloon") originating from [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") is [detected in U.S. airspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Chinese_balloon_incident "2023 Chinese balloon incident"), increasing [tensions between the countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93United_States_relations#Biden_administration_(2021%E2%80%932025) "China–United States relations");
*   Remains of [_Titan_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan_(submersible) "Titan (submersible)"), a [submersible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submersible "Submersible") that [imploded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan_submersible_implosion "Titan submersible implosion") during an expedition to view the [wreck of the _Titanic_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wreck_of_the_Titanic "Wreck of the Titanic");
*   [Azerbaijani soldiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijani_Armed_Forces "Azerbaijani Armed Forces") locked in combat in [Nagorno-Karabakh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagorno-Karabakh "Nagorno-Karabakh") amidst an [Azerbaijani offensive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Azerbaijani_offensive_in_Nagorno-Karabakh "2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh");
*   [Israel invades the Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") in retaliation for the [October 7 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks") by militant group [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas") and [spills over into major parts of the Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Eastern_crisis_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)");
*   [7.8 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Turkey-Syria_earthquake "2023 Turkey-Syria earthquake") strike [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") and [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey"), leaving up to 62,000 dead and 121,000 injured.

**2023** ([MMXXIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_numerals "Roman numerals")) was a [common year starting on Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_year_starting_on_Sunday "Common year starting on Sunday") of the [Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_calendar "Gregorian calendar"), the 2023rd year of the [Common Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Era "Common Era") (CE) and _[Anno Domini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anno\_Domini "Anno Domini")_ (AD) designations, the 23rd year of the [3rd millennium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_millennium "3rd millennium")and the [21st century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st_century "21st century"), and the 4th year of the [2020s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020s "2020s") decade.

Calendar year

Catastrophic natural disasters in 2023 included the [5th-deadliest earthquake of the 21st century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lists_of_21st-century_earthquakes "Lists of 21st-century earthquakes")[striking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Turkey%E2%80%93Syria_earthquakes "2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes")[Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") and [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria"), leaving up to 62,000 people dead; [Cyclone Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Freddy "Cyclone Freddy"), the longest-lasting recorded tropical cyclone in [history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteorological_history_of_Cyclone_Freddy "Meteorological history of Cyclone Freddy") in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"), which led to over 1,400 deaths in [Malawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malawi "Malawi") and [Mozambique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozambique "Mozambique"); [Storm Daniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_Daniel "Storm Daniel"), which became the deadliest tropical cyclone worldwide since [Typhoon Haiyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Haiyan "Typhoon Haiyan") after killing at least 5,300 people in [Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya "Libya"); a major [6.8 magnitude earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Marrakesh%E2%80%93Safi_earthquake "2023 Marrakesh–Safi earthquake") striking western [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco"), killing 2,960 people; and a [6.3 magnitude quadruple earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Herat_earthquakes "2023 Herat earthquakes") striking western [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan"), killing over 1,400 people. The year also saw a decline in the severity of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), with the [WHO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") (World Health Organization) ending its [global health emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_health_emergency_of_international_concern "Public health emergency of international concern") status in May.

The [Russo-Ukrainian war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022%E2%80%93present) "Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)") and [Myanmar civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myanmar_civil_war_(2021%E2%80%93present) "Myanmar civil war (2021–present)") continued in 2023, and a [series of](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_Belt "Coup Belt")[coups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d'%C3%A9tat "Coup d'état"), several armed conflicts, and [political crises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Nigerien_crisis "2023 Nigerien crisis") broke out in numerous African nations, most notably a [Sudanese civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudanese_civil_war_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Sudanese civil war (2023–present)"). In [Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia "Armenia") and [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan "Azerbaijan"), the [Nagorno-Karabakh conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagorno-Karabakh_conflict "Nagorno-Karabakh conflict") ended after over 100,000 [Armenians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians "Armenians")[fled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_of_Nagorno-Karabakh_Armenians "Flight of Nagorno-Karabakh Armenians") the region after an [Azeri military invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Azerbaijani_offensive_in_Nagorno-Karabakh "2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh"). In [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), the year marked the beginning of the [ethnic violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%932025_Manipur_violence "2023–2025 Manipur violence") in the state of [Manipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manipur "Manipur") between the [Kuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuki_people "Kuki people") and the [Meitei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meitei_people "Meitei people") people. A major escalation of the [Israeli–Palestinian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict "Israeli–Palestinian conflict") occurred in October when [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas"), the governing body of the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip"), led [a major attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hamas-led_attack_on_Israel "2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel") on [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"), leading the latter to both [declare war on Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") and [invade the Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_invasion_of_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip"); the Israeli [aerial bombardment campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_bombing_of_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip") killed 20,000 Palestinians within two months and caused a [humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Gaza humanitarian crisis (2023–present)"), leading to [a genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide "Gaza genocide") that formed the basis of an [ICJ case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa's_genocide_case_against_Israel "South Africa's genocide case against Israel") brought by [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") that December.

A [banking crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_United_States_banking_crisis "2023 United States banking crisis") resulted in the collapse of numerous [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") regional banks as well as the [buyout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acquisition_of_Credit_Suisse_by_UBS "Acquisition of Credit Suisse by UBS") of [Credit Suisse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_Suisse "Credit Suisse") by [UBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS "UBS") in [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland"). The two largest American banks to collapse were [Silicon Valley Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Valley_Bank "Silicon Valley Bank") and [First Republic Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Republic_Bank "First Republic Bank"), two of the three largest [banking collapses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_bank_failures_in_the_United_States "List of largest bank failures in the United States") in US history. The most notable of numerous acquisitions in various industries included October's energy acquisitions with [ExxonMobil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExxonMobil "ExxonMobil") and [Chevron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevron_Corporation "Chevron Corporation") buying [Pioneer Natural Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_Natural_Resources "Pioneer Natural Resources") and [Hess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hess_Corporation "Hess Corporation") respectively, the luxury fashion holding company [Tapestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapestry,_Inc. "Tapestry, Inc.") ([Coach New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach_New_York "Coach New York") and [Kate Spade New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York "Kate Spade New York")) announcing its purchase of [Capri Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capri_Holdings "Capri Holdings") (Michael Kors and [Versace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Versace "Versace")), and the closure of [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft")'s [acquisition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acquisition_of_Activision_Blizzard_by_Microsoft "Acquisition of Activision Blizzard by Microsoft") of [Activision Blizzard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activision_Blizzard "Activision Blizzard"). In the realm of technology, 2023 saw [the continued rise of generative AI models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom"), with increasing applications across various industries. These models, leveraging advancements in [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") and [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing"), had become capable of creating realistic and coherent text, music, and images.

*   [January 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_9 "January 9") – [Juliaca massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliaca_massacre "Juliaca massacre"): At least 18 people are killed and over 100 others are injured when the [Peruvian National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_National_Police "Peruvian National Police") fire upon [demonstrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%932023_Peruvian_political_protests "2022–2023 Peruvian political protests") in [Juliaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliaca "Juliaca").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-10)
*   [January 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_10 "January 10")–[17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_17 "January 17") – A [cold snap in Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Afghanistan_cold_snap "2023 Afghanistan cold snap") kills 166 people and nearly 80,000 livestock.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-11)
*   [January 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_15 "January 15") – [Yeti Airlines Flight 691](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeti_Airlines_Flight_691 "Yeti Airlines Flight 691") crashes during final approach into [Pokhara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokhara "Pokhara"), [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal "Nepal"), killing all 72 people on board.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-12)
*   [January 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_16 "January 16") – [Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_War "Tigray War"): [Amharan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amhara_Region "Amhara Region") Special Forces withdraw from the [Tigray Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_Region "Tigray Region") in line with an [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union")-backed [peace agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia%E2%80%93Tigray_peace_agreement "Ethiopia–Tigray peace agreement") between the [Ethiopian government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Ethiopia "Government of Ethiopia") and the [Tigray People's Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_People's_Liberation_Front "Tigray People's Liberation Front").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-13)
*   [January 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_17 "January 17") – [Nguyễn Xuân Phúc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nguy%E1%BB%85n_Xu%C3%A2n_Ph%C3%BAc "Nguyễn Xuân Phúc") resigns as [President of Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Vietnam "President of Vietnam") amid several recent scandals in [the government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Vietnam "Government of Vietnam").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-14)
*   [January 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_18 "January 18") – [A helicopter crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Brovary_helicopter_crash "2023 Brovary helicopter crash") in [Brovary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brovary "Brovary") near [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv"), [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") kills 14 people including [Ukrainian Minister of Internal Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Internal_Affairs_(Ukraine)#Ministers_of_Internal_Affairs "Ministry of Internal Affairs (Ukraine)")[Denys Monastyrsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denys_Monastyrsky "Denys Monastyrsky").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-2023-01-18_BBC-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-17)
*   [January 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_20 "January 20") – The [Parliament of Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Trinidad_and_Tobago "Parliament of Trinidad and Tobago")[elects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Trinidad_and_Tobago_presidential_election "2023 Trinidad and Tobago presidential election") former [senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(Trinidad_and_Tobago) "Senate (Trinidad and Tobago)") president, minister and lawyer [Christine Kangaloo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Kangaloo "Christine Kangaloo") as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Trinidad_and_Tobago "President of Trinidad and Tobago") in a 48–22 vote.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-18)
*   [January 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_21 "January 21")

    *   [Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_War "Tigray War"): [Eritrean forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean_Defence_Forces "Eritrean Defence Forces") withdraw from [Shire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shire,_Ethiopia "Shire, Ethiopia") and other major towns in the [Tigray Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_Region "Tigray Region") of [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-20)

*   [January 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_25 "January 25") – [Chris Hipkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hipkins "Chris Hipkins") succeeds [Jacinda Ardern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacinda_Ardern "Jacinda Ardern") as [Prime Minister of New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_New_Zealand "Prime Minister of New Zealand"),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-January25-21) six days after she announced [her resignation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resignation_of_Jacinda_Ardern "Resignation of Jacinda Ardern").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-22)
*   [January 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_27 "January 27") – Widespread unrest erupts in [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") following an [Israeli military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces "Israel Defense Forces")[raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_2023_Jenin_incursion "January 2023 Jenin incursion") in [Jenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenin "Jenin") the previous day, which killed nine Palestinians. Incendiary air balloons are launched into Israeli-populated areas following it. Israel responds with targeted airstrikes. *   [January 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_27 "January 27")–[28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_28 "January 28") – The second round of the [2023 Czech presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Czech_presidential_election "2023 Czech presidential election") is held, with [Petr Pavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_Pavel "Petr Pavel") declared winner.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-25)
*   [January 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_30 "January 30")

    *   [Prime Minister of Fiji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Fiji "Prime Minister of Fiji")[Sitiveni Rabuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitiveni_Rabuka "Sitiveni Rabuka") confirms that [Kiribati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiribati "Kiribati") will rejoin the [Pacific Islands Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islands_Forum "Pacific Islands Forum") after leaving the organization the previous year.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-29)

### February

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: February")]

*   [February 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_1 "February 1") – [Lebanese liquidity crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_economic_crisis_(2019-present) "Lebanese economic crisis (2019-present)"): The [central bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banque_du_Liban "Banque du Liban") of [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon "Lebanon") devalues the [Lebanese pound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_pound "Lebanese pound") by 90% amid an ongoing [financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_crisis "Financial crisis").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-30)
*   [February 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_2 "February 2")
    *   [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") and [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") announce the finalization of an [agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Sudan_normalization_agreement "Israel–Sudan normalization agreement") to normalize [relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Sudan_relations "Israel–Sudan relations") between the two countries.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-:3-31)
    *   The [European Central Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Central_Bank "European Central Bank") and [Bank of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_England "Bank of England") raise their interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to combat inflation, one day after the [US Federal Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve "Federal Reserve") raises its [federal funds rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_funds_rate "Federal funds rate") by 0.25 percentage points.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-32)

*   [February 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_3 "February 3")
    *   The US announces it is tracking [alleged Chinese spy balloons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Chinese_balloon_incident "2023 Chinese balloon incident") over the Americas, later announcing that the balloons did not collect any information.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-33) One balloon drifts from Yukon to [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") before being shot down the next day, and a second hovers over Colombia and Brazil. This event is followed by subsequent [detections and shootdowns of high-altitude objects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_high-altitude_object_events_in_2023 "List of high-altitude object events in 2023") elsewhere.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-:2-36)
    *   A [Norfolk Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Southern_Railway "Norfolk Southern Railway") train carrying [hazardous materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazardous_materials "Hazardous materials")[derails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Ohio_train_derailment "2023 Ohio train derailment") in [East Palestine, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Palestine,_Ohio "East Palestine, Ohio"). Multiple train cars burn for more than two days, followed by emergency crews conducting a [controlled burn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controlled_burn "Controlled burn") of several additional cars, releasing [hydrogen chloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_chloride "Hydrogen chloride") and [phosgene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosgene "Phosgene") into the atmosphere.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-guardian-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-38)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Tropical_Cyclone_Freddy_near_Madagascar_-_21_February_2023_%2852702958719%29.jpg/250px-Tropical_Cyclone_Freddy_near_Madagascar_-_21_February_2023_%2852702958719%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tropical_Cyclone_Freddy_near_Madagascar_-_21_February_2023_(52702958719).jpg)

[Cyclone Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Freddy "Cyclone Freddy") near Madagascar

*   [February 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_4 "February 4") – [Cyclone Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Freddy "Cyclone Freddy")[forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteorological_history_of_Cyclone_Freddy "Meteorological history of Cyclone Freddy") in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"). It would become the longest lasting [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") in history and [cause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_response_to_Cyclone_Freddy "Humanitarian response to Cyclone Freddy") over 1,400 deaths and countless injuries and property damage across southeastern Africa.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-Records-39)
*   [February 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_5 "February 5") – The [2023 Cypriot presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cypriot_presidential_election "2023 Cypriot presidential election") is held, with [Nikos Christodoulides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikos_Christodoulides "Nikos Christodoulides") elected [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Cyprus "President of Cyprus").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-:123-41)
*   [February 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_6 "February 6") – A 7.8 [M ww](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismic_magnitude_scales#Mww "Seismic magnitude scales")[earthquake strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Turkey%E2%80%93Syria_earthquakes "2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes") southern and central [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") and northern and western [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") followed by a 7.7 M ww aftershock on the same day, causing widespread damage and at more than 59,000 fatalities and 121,000 injured.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-TRdead22/42-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-D_6600-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-TRinjured-44)
*   [February 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_13 "February 13") – The [2023 Bangladeshi presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Bangladeshi_presidential_election "2023 Bangladeshi presidential election") scheduled for 19 February is held, with [Shahabuddin Chuppu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahabuddin_Chuppu "Shahabuddin Chuppu") of the [Awami League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awami_League "Awami League"), the only nominated candidate, elected unopposed.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-49)
*   [February 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_14 "February 14") – The [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") approves a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel [vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle "Vehicle") in the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") from 2035, citing the need to combat [climate change in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Europe "Climate change in Europe") and promote [electric vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_vehicle "Electric vehicle").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-50)
*   [February 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_16 "February 16") – Lawmakers in the [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia")[State Duma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Duma "State Duma") vote to withdraw Russia from 21 conventions of the [Council of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-51)
*   [February 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_17 "February 17") – The [South African Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Navy "South African Navy") hosts a 10-day joint [military exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_exercise "Military exercise") in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean") with [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-52)
*   [February 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_19 "February 19") – [Libyan Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libyan_Crisis_(2011%E2%80%93present) "Libyan Crisis (2011–present)"): The [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") announces the organization of a [peace conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_conference "Peace conference") to address the instability in [Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya "Libya").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-53)
*   [February 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_21 "February 21") – Vladimir Putin announces that Russia is suspending its participation in [New START](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_START "New START"), a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the US.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-54)
*   [February 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_23 "February 23") – [Oman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman "Oman") opens its [airspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airspace "Airspace") to [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")[airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_airlines_of_Israel "List of airlines of Israel") for the first time, in an upgrade of [bilateral relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Oman_relations "Israel–Oman relations").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-55)
*   [February 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_25 "February 25") – [2023 Nigerian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Nigerian_general_election "2023 Nigerian general election"): [Bola Tinubu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bola_Tinubu "Bola Tinubu") is elected as Nigeria's [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Nigeria "President of Nigeria"), defeating former [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_Nigeria "Vice President of Nigeria")[Atiku Abubakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atiku_Abubakar "Atiku Abubakar") and [Peter Obi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Obi "Peter Obi").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-Punch_Newspapers_2023-57)
*   [February 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_27 "February 27") – The United Kingdom and the European Union reach an [agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Framework "Windsor Framework") surrounding modifications to the [Northern Ireland Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_Protocol "Northern Ireland Protocol").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-58)
*   [February 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_28 "February 28") – A [train crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempi_train_crash "Tempi train crash") in [Thessaly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thessaly "Thessaly"), [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece"), kills 57 people and injures dozens. The crash leads to nationwide [protests and strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempi_train_crash_protests "Tempi train crash protests") against the condition of Greek railways and their mismanagement.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-60)

*   [March 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_2 "March 2") – The [National Assembly of Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_of_Vietnam "National Assembly of Vietnam") declares [Võ Văn Thưởng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%B5_V%C4%83n_Th%C6%B0%E1%BB%9Fng "Võ Văn Thưởng") as the country's new president after receiving 98.38% votes from the Vietnamese parliament.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-61)
*   [March 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_4 "March 4")
    *   UN member states agree on a legal framework for the [High Seas Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Seas_Treaty "High Seas Treaty"), which aims to protect 30% of the world's [oceans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean "Ocean") by 2030.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023#cite_note-63)

# Nokia Defense and C3IA partner to accelerate digital transformation across UK defense operations

## Press Release

Summary bullets

*    Partnership combines Nokia Defense's advanced connectivity with C3IA's systems engineering, capability integration and security services expertise to support UK defense modernization.
*   Focuses on delivering resilient multi-domain capabilities spanning tactical communications, C2, sensing, autonomous systems and edge computing.
*   Builds on Nokia Defense and C3IA’s participation in the UK MOD TacSys framework to enhance tactical communications and interoperability.

At the 2026 DVD (Defence Vehicle Dynamics) event, Nokia Defense and C3IA, a UK specialist in systems engineering, capability integration and security services, announced the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration and support the digital transformation of UK Defense. The partnership combines Nokia's expertise in advanced connectivity with C3IA's engineering, capability integration, support and security services to help deliver next-generation defense capabilities for modern, multi-domain operations.

Together, the companies will deliver resilient communications, secure information sharing and network interoperability across land, air, maritime, cyber and space domains. The collaboration also builds on Nokia Defense and C3IA's participation in the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) Tactical Communication Systems (TacSys) framework, providing access to Nokia’s full connectivity portfolio from headquarters to the tactical edge.

Modern military operations increasingly depend on the ability to securely connect people, platforms, sensors and data across multiple domains. Under the agreement, Nokia Defense and C3IA will co-develop solutions across tactical and operational communications, private 4G and 5G, situational awareness, command and control (C2), sensing, autonomous systems and edge computing. The collaboration will focus on translating advanced communications technologies into practical, integrated capabilities that address real operational requirements for the defense sector.

Nokia Defense and C3IA participate in the UK Government’s TacSys framework (RM6393) in Lot 1 (Services) and Lot 3 (Components), giving the UK MOD and other public sector organizations the ability to procure Nokia's connectivity portfolio to support future tactical communications requirements.

Nokia Defense provides secure, intelligent connectivity for defense in the AI era. Built on Nokia’s global leadership across fixed, mobile, and transport networks, it delivers resilient, mission-ready communications solutions that strengthen national security and support critical operations worldwide.

**About Nokia**

Our network solutions span fixed and mobile networks, as well as IP, optical, core, and data center networks. **About C3IA**

C3IA provides technical and security services across both public and private sectors. Specialising in systems engineering, ICT, information assurance, and NCSC-assured cyber services, C3IA plays a pivotal role in supporting the delivery of critical defence programmes. C3IA is dedicated to building long-lasting relationships with our clients, partners and community, delivering exceptional value through our commitment to quality and collaboration.

# Nokia Defense and C3IA partner to accelerate digital transformation across UK defense operations

## Press Release

Summary bullets

*    Partnership combines Nokia Defense's advanced connectivity with C3IA's systems engineering, capability integration and security services expertise to support UK defense modernization.
*   Focuses on delivering resilient multi-domain capabilities spanning tactical communications, C2, sensing, autonomous systems and edge computing.
*   Builds on Nokia Defense and C3IA’s participation in the UK MOD TacSys framework to enhance tactical communications and interoperability.

At the 2026 DVD (Defence Vehicle Dynamics) event, Nokia Defense and C3IA, a UK specialist in systems engineering, capability integration and security services, announced the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration and support the digital transformation of UK Defense. The partnership combines Nokia's expertise in advanced connectivity with C3IA's engineering, capability integration, support and security services to help deliver next-generation defense capabilities for modern, multi-domain operations.

Together, the companies will deliver resilient communications, secure information sharing and network interoperability across land, air, maritime, cyber and space domains. The collaboration also builds on Nokia Defense and C3IA's participation in the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) Tactical Communication Systems (TacSys) framework, providing access to Nokia’s full connectivity portfolio from headquarters to the tactical edge.

Modern military operations increasingly depend on the ability to securely connect people, platforms, sensors and data across multiple domains. Under the agreement, Nokia Defense and C3IA will co-develop solutions across tactical and operational communications, private 4G and 5G, situational awareness, command and control (C2), sensing, autonomous systems and edge computing. The collaboration will focus on translating advanced communications technologies into practical, integrated capabilities that address real operational requirements for the defense sector.

Nokia Defense and C3IA participate in the UK Government’s TacSys framework (RM6393) in Lot 1 (Services) and Lot 3 (Components), giving the UK MOD and other public sector organizations the ability to procure Nokia's connectivity portfolio to support future tactical communications requirements.

# Nokia and KONGSBERG sign agreement to advance defense communications with 5G technology

Summary

*   Collaboration combines the companies’ expertise in tactical communications and mobile networks to deliver advanced capabilities to defense forces and allied nations.
*   Focuses on deployable 5G solutions for field operations today, while exploring future technologies like 6G to boost situational awareness and military readiness

Nokia and Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace (KONGSBERG), Norway’ leading defense technology provider, specializing in advanced systems across land, sea, air, and space domains, today announced the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to collaborate on enhancing tactical communications solutions for the defense sector. The agreement brings together KONGSBERG’s expertise in military tactical communications and Nokia’s leadership in commercial 4G, 5G, and private wireless technologies to deliver secure, resilient, and high-performance networks for defense organizations and allied nations.

The collaboration will aim to simplify the deployment of 5G in tactical systems, enhancing reliable and interoperable battlefield communications. It will also explore opportunities including tactical 5G capabilities, integration with unmanned systems and sensors, and participation in European Defense Fund initiatives like 5G COMPAD and the Federated Advanced Cyber Physical Test Range (FACT) program. Longer term, the companies will look at future technologies such as Nokia’s 6G “network as a sensor” (Integrated Sensing and Communication) to enhance situational awareness and military readiness.

# Nokia and KONGSBERG sign agreement to advance defense communications with 5G technology

Summary

*   Collaboration combines the companies’ expertise in tactical communications and mobile networks to deliver advanced capabilities to defense forces and allied nations.
*   Focuses on deployable 5G solutions for field operations today, while exploring future technologies like 6G to boost situational awareness and military readiness

Nokia and Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace (KONGSBERG), Norway’ leading defense technology provider, specializing in advanced systems across land, sea, air, and space domains, today announced the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to collaborate on enhancing tactical communications solutions for the defense sector. The agreement brings together KONGSBERG’s expertise in military tactical communications and Nokia’s leadership in commercial 4G, 5G, and private wireless technologies to deliver secure, resilient, and high-performance networks for defense organizations and allied nations.

The collaboration will aim to simplify the deployment of 5G in tactical systems, enhancing reliable and interoperable battlefield communications. It will also explore opportunities including tactical 5G capabilities, integration with unmanned systems and sensors, and participation in European Defense Fund initiatives like 5G COMPAD and the Federated Advanced Cyber Physical Test Range (FACT) program. Longer term, the companies will look at future technologies such as Nokia’s 6G “network as a sensor” (Integrated Sensing and Communication) to enhance situational awareness and military readiness.

“

![Image 16: Kjetil R. Myhra, EVP Defence Systems at Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace](https://content.presspage.com/quotes/150_71911.jpg?1198940695)

> “By combining KONGSBERG’s tactical communication assets with Nokia’s leadership in industry-standard technologies, we can speed up the use of civilian telecom solutions in defense. Together, we’ll explore how 5G and 6G can support the developing connectivity requirements in tactical systems, from secure voice and real-time data to unmanned systems and advanced sensors,”

- [Nokia](https://chart.ainvest.com/NYSE-NOK/)[NOK+0.75%](https://www.ainvest.com/stocks/NYSE-NOK/) Defense signed an MoU with UK integrator C3IA to co-develop military communications, but no contract value or timeline was disclosed.

- The agreement formalizes existing ties under the UK MOD's TacSys framework, reducing procurement friction but lacking immediate revenue.

- Nokia's defense [strategy](https://chart.ainvest.com/NASDAQ-MSTR/)[MSTR+16.39%](https://www.ainvest.com/stocks/NASDAQ-MSTR/) includes hardware acquisitions (e.g., Fenix Group) and partnerships for 5G/AI, but the UK deal is a small strategic step.

- Defense remains a niche for Nokia, with AI/cloud infrastructure driving 52% YTD stock gains and €2.8B Q2 order intake.

Nokia Defense signed a [memorandum of understanding with British systems-integrator C3IA at the Defence Vehicle Dynamics trade show on September 16](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nokia-defense-c3ia-partner-accelerate-070000540.html), billed as an effort to "accelerate digital transformation across UK defense operations." On the page it reads as a step into Europe's military-connectivity build-up. In practice it is an MoU — no contract value disclosed, no committed revenue, no delivery schedule — struck between a vendor and an integrator who already sit together on the same UK Ministry of Defence procurement framework.

Ask Aime: How does Nokia's defense deal impact military connectivity in Europe?

That gap between the headline and the ink is the whole story, but not the story the press release wants you to draw. Nokia's defense push is real. This specific item is not yet. Getting the two apart is what matters for anyone deciding how much weight to give the headline.

Ask Aime: How might Nokia's defense push impact its stock price and future growth prospects?

## What was actually signed

A memorandum of understanding is an expression of intent, not an order. The announcement names the ambition — co-developing [tactical and operational communications, private 4G and 5G networks, command-and-control systems, autonomous systems, and edge computing](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/nokia-defense-and-c3ia-in-uk-defense-partnership-ce785bd2db8cf221) across land, air, maritime, cyber, and space — but discloses no money, no timeline, and no committed buy. Kaleidoscope that against what the two companies already have: [Nokia](https://chart.ainvest.com/NYSE-NOK/)[NOK+0.75%](https://www.ainvest.com/stocks/NYSE-NOK/) Defense and C3IA each hold positions under the MOD's [TacSys procurement framework (reference RM6393)](https://kalkine.co.uk/news/announcements/nokia-defense-and-c3ia-sign-mou-to-drive-digital-transformation-across-uk-defence-operations), Nokia on the services lot and both on the components lot. An MoU between two incumbents of the same framework is largely a formalization of a relationship the MOD already sanctions.

That is not nothing. Framework participation is a pre-approved route for the MOD to buy, so this lowers the friction to a future award. But it is route-to-market, not revenue. Until a specific contract drops out of TacSys, the "partnership" is a positioning statement with a handshake.

**A trade-show MoU between two companies already on the same buying framework is a formalized handshake, not a contract.**

## The direction is genuine

Dismissing the weapons of this as pure marketing would be the same error in reverse. Nokia's defense line has independent engineering substance beneath the rhetoric. In May 2024 Nokia closed the acquisition of Fenix Group, a US specialist in tactical broadband communications whose [Banshee and Talon radios](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-successfully-completes-acquisition-of-fenix-group-accelerating-us-strategy/) are real, deployable hardware — a hardware commitment, not a slide. Since then it has stacked integration partners the way its strategy implies: [KNDS for 5G connectivity on vehicles and unmanned systems](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-defense-and-knds-close-critical-connectivity-gap-for-soldiers-and-unmanned-systems/) in June, and NestAI for AI-powered military communications in July. Defense is a stated priority for Nokia's mobile business in part because [NATO tenders shut out Chinese rivals](https://www.facebook.com/LightReading/posts/the-defense-sector-has-emerged-as-a-priority-for-nokias-mobile-business-which-do/1194492349364720/), removing the price-and-trust drag that stalks its commercial business.

So the honest read of the C3IA MoU is: it extends a genuine, well-built strategic line into the UK. The skepticism applies to the size of the moment, not to whether the strategy is real.

## The scale problem

Where the story breaks is proportionate size. Nokia generated [€19.9 billion of net sales](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-03/nokia-annual-report-2025.pdf) in 2025. "Military communication" as an entire global category is a roughly [$37 billion market per one industry estimate](https://www.coherentmarketinsights.com/industry-reports/military-communication-market) — a niche, not a segment that can move a €20 billion company. Nokia does not break out defense revenue separately, which is itself telling: if the line were material to the P&L, it would be a reported segment. A defense MoU without a disclosed value attached to it is, at this scale, a rounding error awaiting a number.

The stock market already told you where the real money is. Nokia's shares have more than doubled over the past year and are up about 52% year to date, and that rally is the AI-infrastructure story, not defense. In the second quarter alone Nokia took [€2.8 billion of AI and cloud order intake](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-report-for-q2-and-half-year-2026/) — nearly three times the prior quarter — while total net sales grew 9% year on year and the Network Infrastructure segment grew 12%. It's the reason the stock trades at roughly 26 times trailing EV/EBITDA with a P/E in the 60s: the market is paying for the pivot to AI data-center networking, and defense is a side bet riding the same connectivity thesis.

**At €19.9 billion of net sales and a $56 billion market cap, a no-value defense MoU is a rounding error in a stock priced for AI order flow.**

The way to use this headline is to confirm a direction, not to chase an event. It confirms that Nokia's military-connectivity line is being built with real partners and real hardware — worth noting as one thread in the company's story. It does not, by itself, change the investment case, because it contains no revenue at all. Treat the announcement as background confirmation of a genuine but small strategic ambition, and keep watching the number the market is actually paying for: the quarterly AI and cloud order intake. That is where this stock's story, and its risk, actually lives.

Nokia Defense signed a [memorandum of understanding with British systems-integrator C3IA at the Defence Vehicle Dynamics trade show on September 16](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nokia-defense-c3ia-partner-accelerate-070000540.html), billed as an effort to "accelerate digital transformation across UK defense operations." On the page it reads as a step into Europe's military-connectivity build-up. In practice it is an MoU — no contract value disclosed, no committed revenue, no delivery schedule — struck between a vendor and an integrator who already sit together on the same UK Ministry of Defence procurement framework.

Ask Aime: How does Nokia's defense deal impact military connectivity in Europe?

That gap between the headline and the ink is the whole story, but not the story the press release wants you to draw. Nokia's defense push is real. This specific item is not yet. Getting the two apart is what matters for anyone deciding how much weight to give the headline.

Ask Aime: How might Nokia's defense push impact its stock price and future growth prospects?

## What was actually signed

A memorandum of understanding is an expression of intent, not an order. The announcement names the ambition — co-developing [tactical and operational communications, private 4G and 5G networks, command-and-control systems, autonomous systems, and edge computing](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/nokia-defense-and-c3ia-in-uk-defense-partnership-ce785bd2db8cf221) across land, air, maritime, cyber, and space — but discloses no money, no timeline, and no committed buy. Kaleidoscope that against what the two companies already have: [Nokia](https://chart.ainvest.com/NYSE-NOK/)[NOK+0.75%](https://www.ainvest.com/stocks/NYSE-NOK/) Defense and C3IA each hold positions under the MOD's [TacSys procurement framework (reference RM6393)](https://kalkine.co.uk/news/announcements/nokia-defense-and-c3ia-sign-mou-to-drive-digital-transformation-across-uk-defence-operations), Nokia on the services lot and both on the components lot. An MoU between two incumbents of the same framework is largely a formalization of a relationship the MOD already sanctions.

That is not nothing. Framework participation is a pre-approved route for the MOD to buy, so this lowers the friction to a future award. But it is route-to-market, not revenue. Until a specific contract drops out of TacSys, the "partnership" is a positioning statement with a handshake.

**A trade-show MoU between two companies already on the same buying framework is a formalized handshake, not a contract.**

## The direction is genuine

Dismissing the weapons of this as pure marketing would be the same error in reverse. Nokia's defense line has independent engineering substance beneath the rhetoric. In May 2024 Nokia closed the acquisition of Fenix Group, a US specialist in tactical broadband communications whose [Banshee and Talon radios](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-successfully-completes-acquisition-of-fenix-group-accelerating-us-strategy/) are real, deployable hardware — a hardware commitment, not a slide. Since then it has stacked integration partners the way its strategy implies: [KNDS for 5G connectivity on vehicles and unmanned systems](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-defense-and-knds-close-critical-connectivity-gap-for-soldiers-and-unmanned-systems/) in June, and NestAI for AI-powered military communications in July. Defense is a stated priority for Nokia's mobile business in part because [NATO tenders shut out Chinese rivals](https://www.facebook.com/LightReading/posts/the-defense-sector-has-emerged-as-a-priority-for-nokias-mobile-business-which-do/1194492349364720/), removing the price-and-trust drag that stalks its commercial business.

So the honest read of the C3IA MoU is: it extends a genuine, well-built strategic line into the UK. The skepticism applies to the size of the moment, not to whether the strategy is real.

## The scale problem

Where the story breaks is proportionate size. Nokia generated [€19.9 billion of net sales](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-03/nokia-annual-report-2025.pdf) in 2025. "Military communication" as an entire global category is a roughly [$37 billion market per one industry estimate](https://www.coherentmarketinsights.com/industry-reports/military-communication-market) — a niche, not a segment that can move a €20 billion company. Nokia does not break out defense revenue separately, which is itself telling: if the line were material to the P&L, it would be a reported segment. A defense MoU without a disclosed value attached to it is, at this scale, a rounding error awaiting a number.

The stock market already told you where the real money is. Nokia's shares have more than doubled over the past year and are up about 52% year to date, and that rally is the AI-infrastructure story, not defense. In the second quarter alone Nokia took [€2.8 billion of AI and cloud order intake](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-report-for-q2-and-half-year-2026/) — nearly three times the prior quarter — while total net sales grew 9% year on year and the Network Infrastructure segment grew 12%. It's the reason the stock trades at roughly 26 times trailing EV/EBITDA with a P/E in the 60s: the market is paying for the pivot to AI data-center networking, and defense is a side bet riding the same connectivity thesis.

**At €19.9 billion of net sales and a $56 billion market cap, a no-value defense MoU is a rounding error in a stock priced for AI order flow.**

The way to use this headline is to confirm a direction, not to chase an event. It confirms that Nokia's military-connectivity line is being built with real partners and real hardware — worth noting as one thread in the company's story. It does not, by itself, change the investment case, because it contains no revenue at all. Treat the announcement as background confirmation of a genuine but small strategic ambition, and keep watching the number the market is actually paying for: the quarterly AI and cloud order intake. That is where this stock's story, and its risk, actually lives.

## Nokia and C3IA deepen UK defence network push

Nokia Defense and UK engineering specialist C3IA will collaborate on tactical communications, private mobile networks, edge computing, sensing, and autonomous systems through a partnership linked to the Ministry of Defence TacSys framework.

September 17, 2026

4 minutes

Read Time

![Image 3: Nokia and C3IA deepen UK defence network push](https://techopia.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/techopia-s19-nokia-c3ia-defence.webp)

Summary
*   Nokia Defense and C3IA have signed an MoU covering tactical communications, command and control, sensing, autonomous systems, and edge computing.
*   Both companies participate in the UK Ministry of Defence TacSys framework, giving eligible public bodies a procurement route into relevant services and components.
*   The agreement is a supplier partnership rather than a newly announced Ministry of Defence contract, and no contract value or deployment programme has been disclosed.

Nokia is expanding its UK defence push through a systems-integration partnership with C3IA, bringing private mobile networks, tactical communications, sensing, autonomous systems, and edge computing into a collaboration already connected to a Ministry of Defence procurement framework.

[Nokia Defense](https://www.nokia.com/) and UK engineering and security specialist C3IA signed a memorandum of understanding at the 2026 Defence Vehicle Dynamics event, with the companies saying they intend to develop integrated communications capabilities for land, air, maritime, cyber, and space operations.

The agreement builds on both companies’ participation in the Ministry of Defence Tactical Communication Systems framework, known as TacSys. Nokia and C3IA are represented on Lot 1 for services and Lot 3 for components, providing a procurement mechanism through which the MOD and other eligible public bodies can buy relevant connectivity capabilities.

No new Ministry of Defence order, programme value, or deployment commitment has been announced alongside the memorandum, so the immediate development is a supplier partnership rather than a contract award. The technological direction is nevertheless clear as military communications move beyond conventional radios towards networks connecting people, vehicles, sensors, computing systems, and autonomous platforms.

## The tactical edge becomes a data problem

Modern defence networks have to move information between systems operating in very different conditions. Headquarters may have access to substantial computing and fixed communications infrastructure, while units at the tactical edge can be working with intermittent connectivity, limited power, constrained spectrum, and equipment that has to continue operating when links to central systems are degraded.

Nokia and C3IA say their work will cover private 4G and 5G, command and control, situational awareness, sensing, autonomous systems, and edge computing. Bringing those components together requires decisions about which information should move, where it should be processed, and how communications continue when parts of the network are unavailable.

Edge computing becomes particularly relevant where sensor or autonomous-system data has to be processed close to where it is generated. Sending every video stream, detection event, or machine decision back to a distant data centre can consume bandwidth and add delay, while loss of the upstream connection can leave a platform unable to perform tasks that depend on remote processing.

Processing selected workloads locally can reduce those dependencies, although it creates another engineering burden. Compute equipment has to be secured, ruggedised where necessary, managed remotely, and integrated with communications and operational systems that may come from several suppliers.

C3IA’s role sits in that integration layer. The company specialises in systems engineering, ICT, information assurance, and security services, while Nokia contributes fixed, mobile, IP, optical, and private-network technology.

## Commercial networks enter specialised environments

Telecommunications vendors have increasingly looked to defence, emergency services, energy, transport, and other mission-critical sectors as private mobile networking has matured. Standards-based 4G and 5G equipment can provide economies of scale and a broad supplier ecosystem, but specialised users still require additional resilience, security, spectrum arrangements, and integration.

That produces a different market from ordinary enterprise private networks. A manufacturer may deploy 5G to connect machinery within a controlled factory, while defence communications may need to operate across moving units, contested spectrum, disconnected environments, or infrastructure that cannot rely on the public telecommunications network.

Nokia’s wider defence strategy has focused on resilient connectivity and tactical communications rather than attempting to turn an off-the-shelf corporate network into a military system with minimal modification. The C3IA agreement extends that strategy in the UK by pairing the network supplier with a domestic engineering organisation already working on defence programmes.

The TacSys framework also shows how technology partnerships interact with procurement. Framework membership does not guarantee an order, but it can reduce the administrative steps required for eligible public-sector customers to buy specified services or components once a need is identified.

Defence estates often contain equipment acquired across several programmes and generations, making replacement of every legacy system commercially and operationally unrealistic. New networking technology therefore has to connect with installed equipment while leaving a path for gradual modernisation.

Autonomous systems increase that pressure because unmanned vehicles and sensors add network endpoints and machine-generated data. Communications infrastructure has to support not only human voice and messaging but software updates, telemetry, command data, video, sensor feeds, and machine-to-machine traffic under conditions where capacity cannot be assumed.

Nokia and C3IA have not disclosed which systems they expect to develop first, nor whether specific MOD programmes are lined up to use the resulting technology. The memorandum should therefore be read as a supplier alignment around future opportunities rather than evidence that a major operational deployment is already under way.

## Nokia and C3IA deepen UK defence network push

Nokia Defense and UK engineering specialist C3IA will collaborate on tactical communications, private mobile networks, edge computing, sensing, and autonomous systems through a partnership linked to the Ministry of Defence TacSys framework.

September 17, 2026

4 minutes

Read Time

![Image 3: Nokia and C3IA deepen UK defence network push](https://techopia.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/techopia-s19-nokia-c3ia-defence.webp)

Summary
*   Nokia Defense and C3IA have signed an MoU covering tactical communications, command and control, sensing, autonomous systems, and edge computing.
*   Both companies participate in the UK Ministry of Defence TacSys framework, giving eligible public bodies a procurement route into relevant services and components.
*   The agreement is a supplier partnership rather than a newly announced Ministry of Defence contract, and no contract value or deployment programme has been disclosed.

Nokia is expanding its UK defence push through a systems-integration partnership with C3IA, bringing private mobile networks, tactical communications, sensing, autonomous systems, and edge computing into a collaboration already connected to a Ministry of Defence procurement framework.

[Nokia Defense](https://www.nokia.com/) and UK engineering and security specialist C3IA signed a memorandum of understanding at the 2026 Defence Vehicle Dynamics event, with the companies saying they intend to develop integrated communications capabilities for land, air, maritime, cyber, and space operations.

The agreement builds on both companies’ participation in the Ministry of Defence Tactical Communication Systems framework, known as TacSys. Nokia and C3IA are represented on Lot 1 for services and Lot 3 for components, providing a procurement mechanism through which the MOD and other eligible public bodies can buy relevant connectivity capabilities.

No new Ministry of Defence order, programme value, or deployment commitment has been announced alongside the memorandum, so the immediate development is a supplier partnership rather than a contract award. The technological direction is nevertheless clear as military communications move beyond conventional radios towards networks connecting people, vehicles, sensors, computing systems, and autonomous platforms.

## The tactical edge becomes a data problem

Modern defence networks have to move information between systems operating in very different conditions. Headquarters may have access to substantial computing and fixed communications infrastructure, while units at the tactical edge can be working with intermittent connectivity, limited power, constrained spectrum, and equipment that has to continue operating when links to central systems are degraded.

Nokia and C3IA say their work will cover private 4G and 5G, command and control, situational awareness, sensing, autonomous systems, and edge computing. Bringing those components together requires decisions about which information should move, where it should be processed, and how communications continue when parts of the network are unavailable.

Edge computing becomes particularly relevant where sensor or autonomous-system data has to be processed close to where it is generated. Sending every video stream, detection event, or machine decision back to a distant data centre can consume bandwidth and add delay, while loss of the upstream connection can leave a platform unable to perform tasks that depend on remote processing.

Processing selected workloads locally can reduce those dependencies, although it creates another engineering burden. Compute equipment has to be secured, ruggedised where necessary, managed remotely, and integrated with communications and operational systems that may come from several suppliers.

C3IA’s role sits in that integration layer. The company specialises in systems engineering, ICT, information assurance, and security services, while Nokia contributes fixed, mobile, IP, optical, and private-network technology.

## Commercial networks enter specialised environments

Telecommunications vendors have increasingly looked to defence, emergency services, energy, transport, and other mission-critical sectors as private mobile networking has matured. Standards-based 4G and 5G equipment can provide economies of scale and a broad supplier ecosystem, but specialised users still require additional resilience, security, spectrum arrangements, and integration.

That produces a different market from ordinary enterprise private networks. A manufacturer may deploy 5G to connect machinery within a controlled factory, while defence communications may need to operate across moving units, contested spectrum, disconnected environments, or infrastructure that cannot rely on the public telecommunications network.

Nokia’s wider defence strategy has focused on resilient connectivity and tactical communications rather than attempting to turn an off-the-shelf corporate network into a military system with minimal modification. The C3IA agreement extends that strategy in the UK by pairing the network supplier with a domestic engineering organisation already working on defence programmes.

The TacSys framework also shows how technology partnerships interact with procurement. Framework membership does not guarantee an order, but it can reduce the administrative steps required for eligible public-sector customers to buy specified services or components once a need is identified.

Defence estates often contain equipment acquired across several programmes and generations, making replacement of every legacy system commercially and operationally unrealistic. New networking technology therefore has to connect with installed equipment while leaving a path for gradual modernisation.

Autonomous systems increase that pressure because unmanned vehicles and sensors add network endpoints and machine-generated data. Communications infrastructure has to support not only human voice and messaging but software updates, telemetry, command data, video, sensor feeds, and machine-to-machine traffic under conditions where capacity cannot be assumed.

Nokia and C3IA have not disclosed which systems they expect to develop first, nor whether specific MOD programmes are lined up to use the resulting technology. The memorandum should therefore be read as a supplier alignment around future opportunities rather than evidence that a major operational deployment is already under way.
